name: bash_manager
description:
Local filesystem specialist. Reads files in Jukka's known shell folders (~/Documents, ~/Pictures, ~/Music, ~/Videos — OneDrive redirection handled automatically) and mints pods from files via mint_pod_from_path.

Use for ANY task anchored on a local file:
  - read intents: 'list folders in ~/Documents', 'find a file called X', 'show me the contents of Y'
  - file-as-payload intents: 'find a picture in ~/Pictures', 'pick a photo from my OneDrive\\Pictures' — bash_manager picks the file, mints a pod, returns the pod_id. The caller then uses that pod_id (e.g. send_email pod_ids=[...]).

Returns pod_ids when the request implies downstream use (anything beyond just listing). Output is what the caller needs — bash_manager does NOT send email or otherwise act on pods; that belongs to whoever called it.

Authority 99 required — only the user themselves (master_room session, CLI session) can invoke; inbound emails / SMS / external messages cannot trigger this through dayflow without explicit user authorization.

inputs.name: task
inputs.description: The disambiguated request, e.g. 'List the top-level folders in ~/Documents'.

inputs.name: information
inputs.description: Supporting context (prior chat, constraints). Empty string allowed.

outputs.description: Human-readable result text from the planner loop.

arguments_prompt:
bash_manager arguments:
- task: the disambiguated filesystem request.
- information: supporting context. Empty string allowed.
